text:
tara: weird onboarding snag. ran the new redwoodctl auto-update (homebrew) on my laptop and my `profiles/localdev.json` got replaced by a default sample. lost localserve route overrides and now our sample app can't hit the emulator. did the updater clobber user files?

sam: ouch. is there a backup file like localdev.json.bak or a migration script? what installer/update version?

tara: updated from 0.10.0 -> 0.10.2. `ls -l ~/.config/redwood/profiles/` only shows `localdev.json` and `sample-app.json`. localdev.json timestamp = update time. no backups.

olivia: that's bad UX. auto-update should never overwrite user config without a safe merge. It should either: 1) migrate keys, 2) write new sample as `sample-app.v0.10.2.json`, or 3) prompt. For a CLI update via brew this is non-interactive so opt 1 or 2.

tara: the file diff shows the new file removed our custom `routes` block and replaced `auth.strategy: local` with `auth.strategy: sample`. that's why localserve fails.

sam: quick workaround: check OS-level file history? On mac, Time Machine might help, but not everyone has it. For immediate fix, re-create the routes and run `redwoodctl localtest --profile localdev` to verify. Also, if you have a container image from yesterday it might include the old profile.

olivia: we should add an auto-backup in the update flow. Installer can run a pre-update hook: if target file exists, copy to `filename.timestamp.bak` and log it to `~/.config/redwood/update-history`. Also CLI should check `update-history` on startup and warn if current profile matches a shipped sample and suggest restore.

tara: filed ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/701 - title: "autoupdate clobbers user profiles; add backup + merge policy". added repro steps: brew upgrade, show file timestamps, diff.

sam: small addition: there are cases where a new sample schema intentionally removes deprecated keys. Merge can't be naive. We should implement a 3-way strategy: user config, shipped sample (old), shipped sample (new) and do a cautious merge preserving unknown keys and logging conflicts for manual resolution. Also provide `redwoodctl restore-profile --from-backup <ts>` to make recovery easy.

olivia: on onboarding side, this hit a new user during our workshop and blocked their progress for 20 mins. We should add a quick check in `redwoodctl init` that warns if the profile matches a shipped sample exactly and offer `--trust` to accept updates.

sam: also worth noting: the updater ran a postinstall script that invoked `redwoodctl init --migrate-samples` which had a bug that used `cp -f` instead of a merge routine. I'll open a PR to change that to `cp -n` (no clobber) and call a migration binary that does the 3-way merge.

tara: for now I restored from our git dotfiles (we keep profiles in a private repo), but not all users do. Can we add a telemetry event when an update overwrites a user profile so we can estimate impact? anonymized boolean + file present would be fine.

olivia: telemetry is fine if opt-in; default opt-out for privacy. But a local `~/.config/redwood/update-history` file is immediate value without sending data. Document it in release notes.

onboarding-bot: NOTE: workshop checklist update suggested: ensure `redwoodctl --version` is 0.10.2+ and run `ls ~/.config/redwood/profiles` before workshop; restore steps: https://interna.redwood/devex/onboarding#profile-recovery

sam: PRs: (1) change postinstall to non-clobber and create backups; (2) add `redwoodctl restore-profile`; (3) add migration lib for merges; (4) add unit tests for brew/homebrew upgrade path. tagging deploy and release leads.

tara: thanks y'all. small but painful bug; appreciate the fast triage. :coffee:
